sa23:1.2: One time, the Buddha was staying at the Squirrels’ Bamboo Grove of Rājagṛha.
sa23:2.1: It was then that Venerable Rāhula visited the Buddha.
sa23:2.2: He bowed his head at the Buddha’s feet, withdrew to sit to one side, and then said to the Buddha,
sa23:2.3: “Bhagavān, what way of knowing and seeing this body of awareness of mine and all the signs of the external world can cause me to have no binding attachments to views about self and what belongs to self or the tendency of self-conceit?”
sa23:3.1: The Bhagavān then said to Rāhula,
sa23:3.2: “Good! It’s good that you can ask the Tathāgata,
sa23:3.3: ‘What way of knowing and seeing this body of awareness of mine and all the signs of the external world can cause me to have no binding attachments to views about self and what belongs to self or the tendency of self-conceit?’ [Is that what you asked?]”
sa23:5.2: “Good! Listen closely! listen closely, and consider it well.
sa23:5.3: I will explain this for you.
sa23:6.1: “Rāhula, you should observe that whatever forms there are, whether they are past, future, or present, internal or external, crude or fine, beautiful or ugly, or distant or near, they are all not self, not different from self, and neither is present in the other.
sa23:6.2: They are correctly observed with equitable wisdom in this way.
sa23:7.1: “Thus, whatever feelings … conceptions … volitions … instances of awareness there are, whether they are past, future, or present, internal or external, crude or fine, beautiful or ugly, or distant or near, they are all not self, not different than self, and neither are present in the other.
sa23:7.2: They are correctly observed with equitable wisdom in this way.
sa23:8.1: “Thus, Rāhula, a monk who knows and sees this body of awareness and all the signs of the external world in this way will have no binding attachments to views of self and what belongs to self or to the tendency of self-conceit.
sa23:9.1: “Rāhula, if a monk has no binding attachments to views of self and what belongs to self or to the tendency of self-conceit regarding this body of awareness and all the signs of the external world, that monk is called one who has stopped craving desires and turned away from the bonds.
sa23:9.2: Right at that moment, he reaches the final end of suffering.”
sa23:10.1: When Rāhula heard what the Buddha taught, he rejoiced and approved.
